thread:
omar: Heads-up — over the last 90m we've seen p95 latency for small embed calls jump from ~120ms to ~420ms. Grafana shows a lot more small requests waiting behind a handful of huge (multi-dim) batches.
jess: ugh. suspected this. are those huge batches from one tenant or lots of tenants?
omar: mostly a single tenant with mixed dims + no preflight. they're sending large arrays that force the splitter to serialize into many backend batches.
kevin: can we detect "small-request" vs "large-batch" earlier and route small ones to a low-latency lane? like weighted-priority routing?
 tara: +1. but need to be careful about fairness and cost — we can't starve throughput customers. How would the API surface the preference? header? route param?
sam: thought: add a non-binding hint header `X-Embed-Pref: latency|throughput` default null. runtime uses it as tiebreaker for routing into a latency-optimized pool (smaller batch window, higher cost).
jess: that sounds reasonable. Ops concerns: we'll need dashboards to show how many requests opt-in and what unit-cost delta is. Also telemetry for fallback decisions.
kevin: telemetry items: routing_decision (latency|default), chosen_pool, batch_size_at_send, queued_ms, fallback_reason (capacity|policy). Sample 100% for latency-pref requests, 1% for others.
tara: console UX: expose a new per-route breakdown: latency-pref% / avg queued_ms / cost_delta. Also a toggle for canary (route_enabled) and a rollout slider.
omar: operational flow: feature-flag the header -> expose canary for 5% tenants -> collect 24h of metrics -> run cost regression on unit price -> if ok, enable 20% -> then GA. Add a soft-fallback so if latency pool is overloaded we fall back to default instead of failing.
sam: we should also consider implicit heuristics: auto-assign small payloads (<1KB or dim_count==1 and n_inputs<8) to latency lane even without header. That helps SDK users who don't set header.
jess: sdk changes: add `preferLatency()` option in client, and add server-side preflight that returns `X-Embed-Estimated-Queue: 30ms` so client can surface expected latency.
kevin: security/abuse: priority hints could be gamed. quota guardrails: only tenants with SLA tier >= "standard" get latency lane, or enforce per-tenant rate cap on latency-pref requests.
tara: rollout checklist: docs, SDK patch, console metric card, quota rules, sampling dashboards, runbook. Who wants to own the console card?
omar: I can sketch the console card (heatmap + trend + cost impact). jess can help with telemetry wiring. kevin on routing impl and fallback. sam on SDK and preflight header.
embed-bot: deploy queued: routing/priority-lane feature-flag scaffold pushed to canary cluster (#deploy-778), ETA for canary test: 2d
jess: perfect. I'll add the dashboard panels and a Prometheus job for `embed_priority_requests_total` with labels. Also we should add an alert if latency-pref queueing > 200ms for 5m.
kevin: one more thing — ensure KV cache affinity: don't split priority and default for same session if we need cache hits. Priority lane should preserve ability to reuse KV cache or fall back gracefully.
omar: good call. We'll add cache-affinity as a rule: if session has open KV cache, prefer same pool, otherwise latency lane allowed.
tara: ok let's sync tomorrow 10am, prep PRs and draft the rollout doc. Thanks all :thumbsup:
